column1: # luals parity expectations: one row per corpus case.
#   case          the .lua file in this directory (without extension)
#   luabox        diag | clean — does `luabox check` (strict) report anything
#                 over the case's file set (the case plus every module its
#                 .deps sidecar names, typechecked as one project)?
#   codes         the sorted, deduped set of LB diagnostic codes `luabox
#                 check --format json` reports for that file set — empty for
#                 a clean row. Asserted exactly, not just "diag" — "not
#                 clean" alone can't distinguish the LB0306 a row names from
#                 an accidental LB0300 or a regressed LB0305 (F19).
#   luals         diag | clean — does lua-language-server --check report any
#                 diagnostic from the type-parity code set (see the script)
#                 anywhere in the SAME file set the luabox column just
#                 typechecked — the case plus its .deps modules, not just
#                 the case's own basename (F17)?
#   note          for AGREE rows, what the case pins; for DIVERGE rows
#                 (luabox != luals), WHY the divergence is intentional. A
#                 DIVERGE row with an empty note is refused by the script
#                 (F28) — this is enforced, not just a convention.
# The two columns are NOT asserted equal — a row where they differ is a
# reviewed, justified divergence, visible in this file rather than buried in
# an allowlist. What the script enforces is that both columns match what is
# written down, so a parity drift in either tool shows up as a diff against
# a claim (the lb0510-matrix discipline, applied to luals parity).
# Measured against lua-language-server 3.13.5 (the version CI pins).
# Corpus rule: luals checks this directory as ONE workspace, so classes are
# workspace-global across cases — every case must use class names unique to
# its own file, or cross-file duplicate-doc-field noise leaks into other
# rows' verdicts. Enforced by the script, not just stated here (F28).
# case
column5: note

column1: clean_control
column5: control: an annotated, well-typed file is clean in both

column1: trailing_nil_param_omitted
column5: #49: omitting a TRAILING `number|nil` param is fine in both (measured, was guessed before)

column1: optional_param_trailing_omitted
column5: #49: `---@param b? number` omitted — the `?` spelling agrees with the `|nil` spelling

column1: nontrailing_nil_param_omitted
column5: #49 residual RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT: g(1) supplies a well-typed p and omits the non-trailing, required q — the ONLY way this can fail is the arity rule, since p is not a type mismatch. luals reports missing-parameter for it, luabox reports LB0301 (arity), matching exactly. (Earlier this fixture called g("only"): a string bound to `p: number|nil` diags in both tools regardless of the arity rule — confounded, could not isolate what it claimed to resolve. F20, measured.)

column1: string_receiver_methods
column5: #48: `s:upper()`, chained `:sub`, `:len` on a string receiver type in both

column1: string_receiver_misspelt
column5: #48: a misspelt string method is undefined-field there, LB0306 here

column1: plain_param_type_mismatch
column5: baseline: string passed to a number param is rejected by both

column1: undefined_field_on_class
column5: baseline: unknown member on a `---@type` instance is rejected by both

column1: duplicate_class_union
column5: #46/#49: two `---@class Config` declarations union their fields in both

column1: duplicate_field_conflict_first_wins
column5: both flag a same-name field re-declared at a different type, by different rules: luals unions (`string|number` fails the number param), luabox keeps the first (LB0311 + LB0300) — divergent semantics, agreeing presence; the semantic divergence is recorded in docs/03-reference/02-limitations.md. LB0311 alone fires regardless of resolution order and can't tell first-wins from last-wins apart (F22) — the codes column is what actually pins it: LB0300 on top of LB0311 only fires because `a`'s kept type is the FIRST declaration's `string`, not the second's `number`; a last-wins resolution would report LB0311 alone

column1: renamed_generic_duplicate
column5: INTENTIONAL DIVERGENCE: lua-language-server 3.13.5 does not support generic classes (`---@class Boxed<T>` yields undefined-doc-name for `T`), while luabox implements them per the LuaCATS generics spec — luabox is deliberately ahead, not lagging; re-measure when the pinned luals version gains support

column1: inherited_member_through_subclass
column5: inheritance: a parent's field types through the subclass in both

column1: inherited_member_misuse
column5: inheritance: misusing an inherited field is rejected by both

column1: string_method_arg_mismatch
column5: #48: `s:rep("three")` argument-checks with the receiver bound in both

column1: required_field_missing_from_literal
column5: a literal missing a required ---@field is rejected by both (LB0300 here, missing-fields there)

column1: required_field_present_in_literal
column5: control: the same literal with the field present is clean in both

column1: carrier_require_typed
column5: #56 end-to-end: a require'd carrier module's declared member types through in both — luals resolves the require as the class, and since #56 so does luabox

column1: carrier_require_undeclared
column5: #56 end-to-end: an undeclared member on the require'd carrier is rejected by both (LB0306 here, undefined-field there)

column1: dynamic_key_carrier_require
column5: #56 narrowing, MEASURED AGAINST THE ORACLE: a member attached to the carrier under a computed key (`H[n] = ...`) exists at runtime but is declared nowhere, and BOTH tools reject the read — undefined-field there, LB0306 here. The narrowing is luals parity, not luabox being stricter; the escape hatch is the next row

column1: dynamic_key_carrier_indexer
column5: the hatch for the row above: `---@field [string] fun(): string` on the class declares the dynamic key space, and the same read is clean in both

column1: generic_carrier_require
column5: a generic `---@class Box<T>` carrier crossing `require` with nothing bound: both reject feeding its member to a `number` param, by different routes — luabox types the unbound parameter `unknown` (naming it, e.g. `---@type Box<number>`, is the action), luals 3.13.5 has no generic classes at all and reports `Cannot assign T to parameter number`. Presence agrees; the rendering is the divergence. NOTE (F21/R29): this row cannot and does not pin the round-1 message-rendering fix (`found T` -> `found unknown`) — both LB0300 either way, so it read diag before and after that change, and no row built on this same "member-type-mismatch on an unbound generic carrier" shape ever could: the fix only changes which placeholder gets rendered inside an already-firing LB0300, and this gate's comparison is diag/clean plus the CODE SET, never message text — a message-only change is structurally invisible at this granularity, not just untested here. The rendering half is pinned at cross_file_require.rs:235 (`generic_carrier_export_never_names_its_unbound_parameter`, asserting the string). The SAME reify_export mechanism (cross as `Ty::Named`, enforced, vs the substituted template, structural and unenforced) has a half that IS falsifiable at diag/clean granularity, and it already has a row for it: generic_carrier_require_undeclared below, where an undeclared-field read flips diag->clean depending on which arm fires. That row is this fix's measurement in this corpus; this row is presence-only corroboration that both tools still reject the well-typed case

column1: generic_carrier_require_bound
column5: INTENTIONAL DIVERGENCE, same root as renamed_generic_duplicate: binding the argument (`---@type Box<number>`) types the required carrier's member here, while luals 3.13.5 cannot parse the generic class at all and reports undefined-field on the member — luabox is deliberately ahead; re-measure when the pinned luals version gains generic-class support

column1: generic_carrier_require_undeclared
column5: INTENTIONAL DIVERGENCE, and the one place #56's enforcement claim does not hold: an UNDECLARED member read off a generic carrier crossing `require` is clean here and undefined-field there. luabox's route is that a class with an unbound parameter crosses as the monomorphised template rather than as `Ty::Named` — which is what stops `T` reaching the consumer (generic_carrier_require) — and a template is structural, so it enforces no member list; luals 3.13.5 has no generic classes at all and treats `GenericBox` as a plain one. Compare carrier_require_undeclared, the same read with the `<T>` dropped, where both report. Pinned in both directions at the type layer too (cross_file_require.rs), where the inherited-parameter cases live as well — a bound `: Base<number>` keeps the class identity and its enforcement, a bare `: Base` does not

column1: metatable_index_carrier_require
column5: #56 narrowing, second shape: a member reached through a `__index` metatable whose source is an undeclared table is not a declaration either, and both tools reject the read across `require` — same rule as dynamic_key_carrier_require, same hatch (declare it on the class, or make the source a declared parent)
